title: Configurable request bundling and SLO mapping for enterprise data-controls
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit a high volume of non-bug data-governance requests (log redaction, retention changes, PII exports, audit exports). Today these requests arrive as independent tickets across Customer Success, Security, and Legal channels, causing duplicated work, inconsistent SLOs, and unclear implementation handoffs. Goals: 1) Provide a structured intake that groups related governance requests into configurable bundles (per-tenant or per-contract) so operators can action them in batches where appropriate. 2) Introduce a deterministic SLO mapping layer so each incoming request is automatically assigned response and implementation SLOs based on request type, customer tier, and regulatory profile. 3) Capture required metadata at intake to remove back-and-forth with Legal/Security and reduce average cycle time. 4) Expose the mapping and bundle state to customers and internal teams via the Console and Linear integration for transparency.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form schema: new governance request form collects required fields (tenant ID, request type from controlled taxonomy, retention window, redaction scope, affected resources, legal justification, export format and purpose, requester contact and ATO level).
Automated routing: requests are programmatically routed to the correct team queue (Security, Legal, Infra Ops, or Customer Success) based on taxonomy and customer tier, with clear owner assigned.

Bundle behavior: admins can opt-in tenant-level bundling; system groups compatible requests into a bundle if they share tenant and compatible timeframe/impact flags; bundle view exists in Console and shows member requests and overall bundle SLO.

SLO mapping: mapping rules engine assigns 'response SLO' (acknowledge) and 'implementation SLO' (complete) at intake. Mapping is configurable via a simple rule editor in Console for Enterprise admins and internal PM/CS teams.
Audit trail: every request and bundle has an immutable audit log (submitter, timestamps, routing decisions), surfaced in Console and exportable via CSV/JSON for compliance review.
Operational playbook: documented runbook for CS/Eng/Legal including escalation path, minimum required artifacts, and checklist for redaction and retention tasks.
Metrics: dashboards show average time-to-acknowledge and time-to-complete by request type and customer tier; a sample dashboard is added to Console default reporting.
Customer communication templates: canned responses for acknowledge, update, and completion states exist and can be customized per customer-tier.
Security sign-off: security/privacy team has vetting step in workflow for PII exports with explicit checklist; security_review_required flag blocks implementation until passed.
Integration: Linear ticket created/updated for each request and bundle with links to Console artifacts and any GH PRs or infra changes.
Pilot: feature is validated in pilot with 2 enterprise customers and reduces average end-to-end cycle time for governance requests by at least 30% vs baseline.
tasks: Finalize taxonomy for governance request types (redaction, retention, PII export, audit export, policy exception).
Design intake form and Console UX for bundle management and SLO rule editor (hand off to Design).
Implement backend: request model, bundle grouping engine, SLO rule engine, and audit log storage.
Routing and notifications: implement routing logic, queue assignment, and notification templates for CS/Legal/Security/Eng.
Add dashboards and metrics to Console; wire telemetry for time-to-ack and time-to-complete per request type/tier.
Create operational runbook and customer-facing templates; train CS and Solutions teams for pilot.
Pilot with two customers, collect feedback, and iterate on taxonomy and SLO rules.
Finalize security/privacy review steps and compliance exports (CSV/JSON) for audits.
